title: Mitochondrial electron transport and oxidative phosphorylation

nodes.label: Complex I (NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase)
nodes.rationale: The FMN site forms a flavin semiquinone during turnover and is a known superoxide-producing leak site, and the Fe/S chain performs sequential one-electron transfers — both of the physical routes the radical-pair and hyperfine arguments require. No published experiment has applied a near-null field and measured plant complex I activity, so this is a hypothesis with a mechanism, not a result.
nodes.caveat: Electron transfer along the Fe/S chain is fast relative to plausible singlet-triplet mixing times, so a coherent radical-pair effect here is harder to argue than at the flavin. Treat the flavin and the cluster chain as separate hypotheses rather than one.

nodes.label: Complex I FMN site
nodes.rationale: A one-electron-reduced flavin is the best-characterised magnetosensitive species in biology; the same chemistry underlies the cryptochrome radical-pair model. The review's argument is precisely that this chemistry is not confined to photoreceptors.

nodes.label: Complex II (succinate dehydrogenase)
nodes.rationale: Carries all three cluster types plus a covalent flavin, and sits at the junction the review nominates as the bottleneck — a change here propagates into both TCA flux and respiratory electron flow.

nodes.label: Alternative NAD(P)H dehydrogenases (NDA/NDB)
nodes.rationale: FAD-dependent, so the same flavin semiquinone chemistry applies. Included mainly as the second confounder alongside AOX — a plant can route around a complex I lesion, which blunts any phenotype and must be controlled for.

nodes.label: Ubisemiquinone (UQ·−)
nodes.rationale: A free-radical intermediate held in a protein pocket. If any respiratory species supports spin-correlated chemistry, this is the leading candidate.

nodes.label: Rieske [2Fe-2S] centre (complex III)
nodes.rationale: The Qo site generates a kinetically stabilised ubisemiquinone — a genuine, comparatively long-lived organic radical in a defined protein pocket, which is the most favourable setting for a field-dependent branching effect anywhere in the respiratory chain.
nodes.caveat: Qo-site semiquinone is short-lived and its occupancy is debated; a field effect here would be easier to argue if lifetime were measured under the relevant conditions.

nodes.label: Cytochrome c
nodes.rationale: A one-electron heme carrier, paramagnetic in the ferric state. Included because Racca et al. place cytochrome c on the path from mitochondrial state to germination timing, which is the developmental window the review argues matters most.

evidence.claim: Cytochrome c and the transcription factor ABI4 link mitochondrial status to ABA-dependent seed germination.

nodes.label: Complex IV (cytochrome c oxidase)
nodes.rationale: The review names cytochrome oxidase explicitly as a candidate direct metabolic target. The heme a3/CuB centre passes through paramagnetic oxygen intermediates (P, F, oxoferryl) whose spin states are, in principle, field-addressable.
nodes.caveat: Strongly exchange-coupled metal centres relax very fast, which argues against coherent spin effects. This is a mechanistically attractive but physically demanding hypothesis, and is labelled T3 for that reason.

nodes.label: Mitochondrial superoxide / H2O2
nodes.rationale: Not a magnetosensitive mechanism itself — it is the amplifier. A field effect too small to measure as a rate change can still register here, because ROS signalling is threshold-like.

evidence.claim: Near-null magnetic field exposure alters ROS-associated transcriptomic and metabolomic programmes in Arabidopsis.
Reactive oxygen species and mitochondria jointly regulate seed germination, establishing the route from mitochondrial ROS to a developmental outcome.

nodes.label: Aconitase (ACO1/2/3)
nodes.rationale: The review nominates aconitase as the sentinel of Fe/S integrity, and the biochemistry supports it: the exposed cluster iron makes aconitase the first TCA activity to fall under oxidative stress, so it reports cluster damage before anything else does.
nodes.caveat: Precisely because aconitase responds to any oxidative insult, a change under NNMF would NOT by itself implicate a magnetic mechanism. It is a sensitive readout and a poor discriminator; it needs a paired ROS-independent control.

nodes.label: Lipoyl synthase (LIP1)
nodes.rationale: A radical-SAM enzyme generating a 5'-deoxyadenosyl radical from a [4Fe-4S] cluster — genuine organic radical chemistry on an iron-sulfur centre, which is the tightest coupling of the review's two proposed mechanisms found anywhere in primary metabolism. Its product lipoylates pyruvate dehydrogenase and the 2-oxoglutarate dehydrogenase complex, so a defect propagates straight into TCA flux.
nodes.caveat: The radical is generated inside the active site and quenched within one turnover; whether a spin-correlated pair with a long enough lifetime to be field-sensitive ever forms is untested.
